title: Trump Urges Calls to Senator Cotton Over Daylight Saving Time
summary:
On Saturday, October 3, President Donald Trump urged Americans to contact Arkansas Senator Tom Cotton about a plan to keep daylight saving time all year. Cotton repeated his opposition to the plan.

Daylight saving time is the period from spring to fall when most parts of the United States set clocks one hour ahead of standard time. Most people change their clocks twice each year. Some states do not follow daylight saving time.

A bill called the Sunshine Protection Act passed the House of Representatives in July. It still faces opposition in the Senate, so the proposed change has not become law.

Supporters, including the White House, say the plan would place more daylight in the hours when people are active. Trump also says changing clocks around the house is troublesome.

Opponents say keeping that clock setting through winter would mean later sunrises by the clock. Cotton says he is concerned about children going to school in darkness. Other opponents also worry about children waiting for school buses and parents driving to work.

The proposal would let states choose not to take part if their lawmakers acted before it became law. The debate concerns which hours should line up with daylight, including time for evening activities and morning travel.
why_it_matters: The proposal concerns when daylight falls during evening activities and children's morning trips to school.
